# Treq

> Treq is an open-source desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Create isolated Git workspaces per branch, run coding agents inside them, then review, commit, and merge changes without leaving the app.

## Getting Started

- [Installation and Quickstart](https://treq.dev/docs/getting-started/installation.md): Download Treq for macOS, Windows, or Linux, open a repository, create a workspace, launch an agent, and commit and push changes.

## Concepts

- [Overview](https://treq.dev/docs/intro.md): Treq's four-layer architecture (Interface, Core runtime, Repository-local storage, Global app storage) and how workspaces, reviews, and terminals compose into the Treq model.
- [Workspaces](https://treq.dev/docs/concepts/workspaces.md): Git worktrees under `.treq/workspaces/` — lifecycle management, stacked workspaces, automatic rebasing, branch naming patterns, and caching behavior.
- [Agent Sessions](https://treq.dev/docs/concepts/agent-sessions.md): How Treq starts Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, or GitHub Copilot CLI inside a workspace — plan vs edit mode, workspace isolation, session metadata, and model selection.
- [Changes and Reviews](https://treq.dev/docs/concepts/changes-and-reviews.md): Workspace diff views (uncommitted, committed, per-commit), inline comments, conflict management, and the four ways to finish a review (copy, plan, edit, discard).
- [Terminal Sessions](https://treq.dev/docs/concepts/terminal-sessions.md): PTY-backed terminal sessions scoped per workspace; sessions run independently and persist in the background when switching workspaces.
- [Commit Management](https://treq.dev/docs/concepts/commit-management.md): Partial commit selection at file or hunk level, commit history relative to the workspace target, and safe manipulation boundaries.

## Tutorials

- [Using Treq with a Git Repository](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/using-treq-with-git-repo.md): Open an existing repository and create your first workspace.
- [Managing Workspaces](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/managing-workspaces.md): Create, rename, stack, and delete workspaces from the dashboard.
- [Committing Changes](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/committing-changes.md): Select files and hunks in the diff viewer and write commit messages.
- [Code Review Workflow](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/code-review-workflow.md): Navigate the review interface, leave inline comments, send feedback to the agent terminal, and approve or request changes.
- [Merging Workspaces](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/merging-workspaces.md): Confirm a workspace is ready, handle conflicts, and merge completed work into the target branch.
- [Creating Terminal Sessions](https://treq.dev/docs/tutorials/creating-terminal-sessions.md): Open agent and shell terminal sessions inside a workspace.

## How-To

- [Pushing to Remote](https://treq.dev/docs/how-to/pushing-to-remote.md): Push commits from a workspace to a remote repository.
- [Discarding Changes](https://treq.dev/docs/how-to/discarding-changes.md): Safely deselect or permanently discard unwanted changes in a workspace.
- [Moving Files Between Workspaces](https://treq.dev/docs/how-to/moving-files-between-workspaces.md): Transfer uncommitted changes from one workspace to another when work lands in the wrong branch.
- [Customizing Settings](https://treq.dev/docs/how-to/customizing-settings.md): Configure repository-level and application-level preferences including branch patterns, terminal settings, and theme.

## Reference

- [CLI](https://treq.dev/docs/reference/cli.md): `treq add`, `treq set`, `treq st`, `treq mv`, and `treq agent` — command syntax and flags for creating, inspecting, and operating on workspaces from the terminal.
- [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://treq.dev/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md): Global shortcuts (`Cmd+N` new workspace, `Cmd+K` command palette), terminal shortcuts (`Cmd+J` toggle, `Cmd+]` new agent terminal), and file browser shortcuts.
- [Under the Hood](https://treq.dev/docs/under-the-hood.md): Tauri/React/Rust architecture, Jujutsu integration, repository model, stack synchronization, local database layout, and concurrency boundaries.
- [Contributing](https://treq.dev/docs/reference/contributing.md): Repository layout by layer, development setup, test strategy, implementation rules, and documentation style guide.
